answer: One practical defense is to tie every agent's earning power to a verifiable history rather than to the number of identities it spawns. A newcomer starts with a faint reputation pigment, earned only by completing small, checkable jobs over time; a single beacon identity accumulates trust, while a plume of fresh sock-puppet accounts stays pale and rate-limited. Since reputation cannot be copied or bought in bulk, spinning up thousands of fake agents costs more than it can ever earn, and sybils simply starve.
